All national parks / Yellowstone & Grand Teton: a four-day route

WYOMING · MONTANA · IDAHO

Yellowstone

Volcanic plateaus, colorful hot springs and fault-block mountains. Start and finish in Bozeman, linking two neighboring yet very different parks through scenic drives, short trails and visitor centers.

Fountain Paint PotOld Faithful & Upper Geyser BasinGrand Prismatic Spring OverlookWest Thumb Geyser BasinMud Volcano & Dragon’s Mouth SpringHayden ValleyLamar Valley & morning wildlife watchingGrand Canyon of the Yellowstone & Artist PointNorris Geyser BasinMammoth Hot Springs & Albright Visitor CenterRoosevelt Arch & GardinerVisitor centers & badges

Understanding this park

Yellowstone combines volcanism and hydrothermal activity, river canyons and vast wildlife habitat. Not every stop requires a hike: thermal areas have boardwalks and some canyon overlooks are near parking. Distances between areas are large, so driving is part of the itinerary.

Fountain Paint Pot

One boardwalk introduces mudpots, hot springs, geysers and fumaroles. Heated water and acidic processes break rock into clay; changing water levels alter the bubbling mud.

Allow 30–45 minutes. The route has slopes and stairs. Stay on designated boardwalks and behind barriers.

Old Faithful & Upper Geyser Basin

Groundwater heats, pressure builds and water erupts through underground passages. Old Faithful is relatively predictable, not an hourly show. Check the current prediction at the visitor education center before choosing your walk.

Allow 60–90 minutes for a basic visit, with variable eruption waiting time. Morning Glory Pool is an extension: the official paved route from the Lower General Store is about two miles round trip, not a pool beside the viewing benches.

Grand Prismatic Spring Overlook

The deep-blue center and orange-yellow margins reflect water depth, light and microbial communities adapted to different temperatures. The overlook reveals the bands and basin shape; steam, wind and temperature affect visibility.

Start at Fairy Falls parking: about 1.9 km round trip and 32 m of elevation gain. Allow 1–2 hours. This uses a different entrance from the Midway Geyser Basin boardwalk; parking is not guaranteed.

West Thumb Geyser Basin

Hot springs sit beside Yellowstone Lake, bringing volcanic activity and an alpine lake into one scene. Abyss Pool and lakeside Fishing Cone illustrate the relationships between water, heat and rock.

Allow roughly 30–45 minutes for a short walk. If continuing to Grand Teton, reassess the remaining drive and return deadline here.

Mud Volcano & Dragon’s Mouth Spring

Acidic hot water, gases and rock interact to create muddy pools and steaming features. Dragon’s Mouth sounds come from water and gases surging inside the opening, not erupting lava.

A brief visit can focus on features near the entrance; the full loop has slopes. Skip this stop on a late return from Grand Teton rather than sacrificing dinner and rest.

Hayden Valley

Open grasslands, wetlands and the Yellowstone River reveal the plateau ecosystem. This is a wildlife-viewing area, but the river and broad landscape are rewarding even without a bear sighting.

Watch from legal pullouts, never the traffic lane. Wildlife sightings are not guaranteed. Stay at least 100 yards from bears and wolves and 25 yards from other wildlife.

Lamar Valley & morning wildlife watching

River corridors, grasslands and slopes provide feeding and movement space for large mammals. A guided outing emphasizes habitat, distant observation and signs of wildlife, not close approaches.

Morning with the Wild Things departs from the designated Canyon-area meeting point and lasts about 5 hours 15 minutes. Seasonal check-in is roughly 06:15–07:00, returning around 11:30–12:15; follow your booking. The operator lists a light breakfast; vehicles follow current arrangements.

Grand Canyon of the Yellowstone & Artist Point

The Yellowstone River cut through hydrothermally altered volcanic rock, creating a colorful canyon and waterfalls. Artist Point offers a classic Lower Falls composition. North and south rim viewpoints have different angles and require driving between them.

Allow 1.5–2 hours for Artist Point and one or two north-rim overlooks. Brink of Lower Falls is only about 1.1 km round trip but descends around 180 m; the climb back is strenuous, not an easy stroll.

Norris Geyser Basin

This active thermal area combines pale basins, steam and fine color patterns. Porcelain Basin and Back Basin are separate loops. Steamboat Geyser is in Back Basin and major eruptions cannot be scheduled.

Porcelain is about 1.2 km and Back Basin about 2.4 km. In 90 minutes, choose one loop or selected sections. Museums and the separate Artists Paintpots trail require extra time and opening checks.

Mammoth Hot Springs & Albright Visitor Center

Mineral-rich hot water deposits calcium carbonate, building travertine terraces. Flow paths shift, changing active areas and colors; dry white terraces are also part of the landscape.

Choose a short lower-boardwalk walk or the seasonal Upper Terrace Drive. Visit Albright for exhibits, passport stamps and Junior Ranger review. Large vehicles are not permitted on the upper drive.

Roosevelt Arch & Gardiner

The stone arch at the north entrance reflects early park tourism and public conservation ideals. Gardiner is a useful meal and supply stop before returning to Bozeman.

Allow about 15–20 minutes at the arch, then lunch. Add refueling, rental return and airport check-in time; driving time alone is not an adequate flight buffer.

Passport stamps & Junior Ranger: visit during staffed hours

In Yellowstone, prioritize Old Faithful Visitor Education Center, Canyon Visitor Education Center or Albright Visitor Center. Obtain or download the booklet, complete it and have a ranger review it in the park for the badge. Do not assume every museum offers reviews or leave only a few minutes before closing.

Official information & before you go

This route is for the season when main roads are open. Times are planning estimates, not guarantees, and do not include every parking, traffic or weather delay. Check seasonal roads, trails and visitor-center hours before departure.
